name: Gmsh
summary: Geometry construction, mesh generation and post-processing through a desktop interface or scripting APIs, useful for building reproducible CFD meshes and preparing parametric geometry studies.
access_note: Canonical development is on ONELAB GitLab. The official site documents GPLv2-or-later terms with a linking exception and separate commercial licensing options.

name: Basilisk
summary: Provides adaptive Cartesian PDE solvers, interface methods and a large collection of reproducible examples. Its native site combines source, documentation, tests and researcher-contributed simulation cases.
access_note: Canonical source is distributed through Darcs. Use the official project pages and source history rather than an arbitrary GitHub mirror.

name: OpenFOAM (OpenCFD distribution)
summary: Provides the OpenCFD distribution of OpenFOAM with solver, model, meshing and post-processing documentation. Identify this distribution explicitly when choosing compatible tutorials, extensions and case files.
access_note: GPLv3 distribution distinct from the OpenFOAM Foundation edition. Follow the official download and version-specific documentation; its development repositories moved to GitLab.com.

name: Palabos
summary: Provides a lattice-Boltzmann framework for research and engineering flow applications. Its official site links the current source repository, documentation and examples covering interfaces, particles and porous media.
access_note: Official source is hosted on GitLab and distributed under AGPLv3. Applications generally require programming rather than a turnkey graphical interface.

name: waLBerla
summary: Combines lattice-Boltzmann flow modeling, particle dynamics, moving geometries and code generation in a parallel multiphysics framework. Useful for constructing coupled flow applications on structured block grids.
access_note: Official project states GPLv3; its maintained source is on the project GitLab server. Select models and generated kernels appropriate to the target hardware.

name: OpenLB
summary: Provides a modular lattice-Boltzmann library with examples spanning engineering flow, thermal transport, particles and porous media. The official user guide documents model setup and execution.
access_note: The official project overview states GPLv2 for code. Documentation has separate GNU Free Documentation License terms; use the official release package.

name: TrioCFD
summary: Documents the CEA turbulent-flow application built on TRUST, including thermal hydraulics, front tracking and fluid-structure models. Useful for understanding its model hierarchy and application scope.
access_note: Source-only distribution now hosted on GitLab. Follow the versioned official documentation and compile against the required TRUST environment.

name: OpenGeoSys
summary: Models coupled thermal, hydraulic, mechanical and chemical processes in porous and fractured media. Offers subsurface-flow workflows, benchmark documentation and examples relevant to groundwater and geothermal research.
access_note: BSD-3-Clause project with active source hosted on its GitLab server. The old ufz/ogs GitHub repository explicitly directs users away from that stale location.

name: Turbulence Modeling Resource
summary: Documents RANS turbulence-model variants alongside verification grids, grid-convergence examples and fundamental validation cases. Helps distinguish implementation errors from the modeling limits of a turbulence closure.
access_note: Moved from NASA Langley to the TMBWG site in February 2026, as confirmed by NASA. Some large files have separate NASA-hosted download locations.

name: ERCOFTAC Knowledge Base Wiki
summary: Organizes CFD application challenges, underlying flow regimes and practice guidance. Useful for understanding a case context, reviewing modeling limitations and locating documented industrial or canonical comparisons.
access_note: ERCOFTAC advertises the wiki as free to visitors; individual test-data packages can have separate access and citation arrangements.

name: ERCOFTAC Classic Collection
summary: Indexes the original ERCOFTAC collection of flow test cases, experimental data and computational comparisons. Includes case descriptions and literature connections useful for selecting established validation exercises.
access_note: The official ERCOFTAC portal describes open access; inspect each dataset, its current hosting location and citation requirements.

name: Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database
summary: Offers queryable numerical turbulence fields through web services and data subsets. Useful for investigating velocity statistics, derivatives, particle trajectories and learning methods without storing complete simulations locally.
access_note: Follow dataset-specific citation and access instructions. Web-service limits, authentication requirements and storage formats vary; API clients are separate from the underlying data.

name: Engine Combustion Network
summary: Collects documented spray and engine experiments with common operating conditions, injector geometry and measured quantities. Supports comparative assessments of injection, mixing, ignition, flame stabilization and soot models.
access_note: Read each experiment's definitions, uncertainty, operating conditions and citation instructions. Matching a named Spray A or Spray G case requires more than reproducing nominal pressure and temperature.

name: University of Texas turbulence data
summary: Provides downloadable DNS statistics and supporting information for turbulent channel and Couette flows. Useful for checking wall-scaled profiles, stresses and other canonical turbulence statistics.
access_note: Read the README accompanying each Reynolds-number dataset and cite the associated papers. These statistics describe specific DNS configurations rather than arbitrary wall-bounded flows.

name: Turbulent Non-Premixed Flames Workshop data
summary: Collects experimental turbulent-flame datasets with scalar and velocity measurements in documented configurations. Supports comparisons of combustion submodels across piloted jets, bluff bodies, swirl and hydrogen flames.
access_note: Providers explicitly request reading documentation and referenced papers, including uncertainty information. The workshop does not guarantee the accuracy of every contributed dataset.

name: NASA NPARC verification and validation archive
summary: Provides example, verification and validation cases associated with Wind-US, alongside broader CFD assessment guidance. Useful for learning how numerical checks and experimental comparisons answer different questions.
access_note: A maintained-access legacy archive with cases from different periods; check case dates, solver assumptions and source-data terms before reuse.

name: Drag and Aeroelastic Prediction Workshops
summary: Provides common aerodynamic geometries, experimental data, grids and comparison protocols for transonic drag and aeroelastic studies. Useful for separating mesh, numerical, turbulence-model and deformation effects.
access_note: Workshop participation and data use are different activities. Follow the selected edition's geometry, data, submission and citation requirements; do not mix results across configurations.

name: AIAA CFD High-Lift Prediction Workshop
summary: Collects standardized high-lift aircraft test cases, geometry, grids and comparison results. Helps researchers assess difficult separated-flow predictions around deployed slats and flaps under shared conditions.
access_note: Use the correct workshop edition and configuration. Individual geometry and experimental files may carry their own attribution, distribution and interpretation requirements.
